chunks: Mūsā ibn Bakr narrated from al-Fuḍayl, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Regarding a man upon whom there is the fasting of a month, and he fasted fifteen days of it, then some matter occurred to him, he said: “If he has fasted fifteen days, then he may make up what remains. But if he has fasted less than fifteen days, it does not suffice him until he fasts a complete month.”

key_terms.خَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ يَوْماً: fifteen days; the threshold that determines the ruling
key_terms.شَهْراً تَامّاً: a complete month; the full period that must be fasted anew
key_terms.شَهْرٍ: a month; the full period of the fasting obligation
key_terms.صَوْمُ: sawm; the required fasting obligation being discussed
key_terms.عَرَضَ لَهُ أَمْرٌ: something occurred to him; an intervening circumstance that interrupts the fast
key_terms.لَمْ يُجْزِئْهُ: it does not suffice him; it is not legally valid enough to count
key_terms.يَقْضِيَ: to make up; to complete the remaining missed days later

ai.seo_question: If someone obligated to fast a month is interrupted after some days, when can he make up the rest and when must he restart the full month?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on an obligated month of sawm when an interruption occurs after part of it has been completed. It establishes that completing fifteen days allows the remainder to be made up later, while completing fewer than fifteen days does not suffice and requires fasting a full month anew.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2005 - Musa ibn Bakr narrated from Al-Fudayl, from Abu Abdullah (as), regarding a man obligated to fast for a month who completed fifteen days of fasting and then was interrupted by some matter.

Imam (as) said: "If he has fasted fifteen days, he may make up the remaining days. However, if he has fasted less than fifteen days, it will not suffice him, and he must start anew and fast a complete month."
